title: React Native GPUI desktop app configuration
description: The desktop/desktop.json file of a React Native GPUI app. Every field is optional: an app with no desktop.json runs and packages with the defaults.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, for editor completion.

productName.description: The name a person sees: window title bar, Dock, menu bar, installers. Defaults to the app's displayName, else its name.

identifier.description: The reverse-DNS bundle id, e.g. com.example.myapp. Defaults to an id derived from the app name.

version.description: The app version. Defaults to the version in package.json.

icon.description: One square PNG, recommended 1024x1024, relative to desktop/. Per-OS icon formats are generated from it. When this is unset the CLI uses its own placeholder, so every packaging format can be built.

title.description: The title bar text. Defaults to productName.

width.description: The window width in points. Defaults to 1024.

height.description: The window height in points. Defaults to 768.

position.description: Where the window opens. Omit to let the platform place it.

resizable.description: Whether the window can be resized. Defaults to true.

restoreState.description: Whether the window remembers its size and position between launches. Defaults to true.

titleBar.description: How the window's title bar is drawn. 'default' keeps the platform's; 'transparent' keeps the window's chrome but lets the app draw under it, which on macOS leaves the traffic lights over the app's own bar; 'hidden' removes it entirely, and the app must draw and move its own bar. On Linux 'transparent' and 'hidden' both ask the compositor for client-side decorations, and a window manager that refuses leaves the native title bar in place. Defaults to 'default'.

trafficLightPosition.description: Where the macOS traffic lights sit inside a transparent or hidden title bar, in points from the window's top-left corner. Ignored on Windows and Linux, which have no traffic lights. Defaults to the platform's own position.

menuBar.description: Whether the main window shows a menu bar. Windows and Linux draw one inside the window; on macOS this does nothing, because the bar belongs to the system. Defaults to true.

devMenu.description: Whether the development menu is available. Defaults to true in development builds.

tray.description: A menu-bar or notification-area icon for the app.

component.description: The React component to render as the tray popover.

icon.description: The tray icon, a PNG or JPEG path relative to desktop/. Without one the tray shows a built-in glyph.

iconTemplate.description: macOS: draw the icon as a template the menu bar tints for light and dark mode. Use it for a monochrome glyph. Defaults to false.

accessory.description: Whether the app runs as an accessory, with no Dock icon. Defaults to true.

targets.description: The formats to build. 'all' means every alpha format for the current OS.

resources.description: Extra files to ship, relative to desktop/.

copyright.description: The copyright line shown by installers.

category.description: The app category, for the Linux desktop entry.

minimumSystemVersion.description: The oldest macOS the app supports. Defaults to 13.0.

entitlements.description: A path to an entitlements plist, relative to desktop/.

infoPlist.description: Extra keys merged into the generated Info.plist.

installMode.description: Whether the installer installs for the current user or for everyone.
